verses.text: Concerning Nineveh, this is the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The Lord is a jealous and avenging God; the Lord is avenging and wrathful; the Lord takes vengeance on His adversaries and keeps wrath for His enemies.
The Lord is slow to anger and great in power, and the Lord will not leave the guilty unpunished; His way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust of His feet.
He rebukes the sea and makes it dry; He dries up all the rivers; Bashan and Carmel wither, and the bloom of Lebanon wilts.
The mountains quake before Him, the hills melt, and the earth heaves before Him, the world and all who dwell in it.
Who can stand before His indignation? Who can endure the heat of His anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken into pieces by Him.
The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; He knows those who take refuge in Him.
But with an overflowing flood, He will make a complete end of the adversaries, and will pursue His enemies into darkness.
What do you conspire against the Lord? He will make a complete end; trouble will not rise up a second time.
Though they are entwined together as thorns, and while drunkards are drunken, they shall be consumed like stubble fully dried.
He who thinks evil against the Lord, and devises wickedness, has turned away from you.
Thus saith the Lord: Though there be mighty men and many, they shall be cut off; yet He shall not be dismayed. I am troubled, but from henceforth I shall not be troubled.
Even now I shall take your crown from you, and I shall destroy your idols.

And the Lord has mourned for you, that from henceforth no one shall remember your name; I shall destroy the graven image that was made from the house of your gods, and I shall cast away your sepulcher. You are indeed a curse, and I shall make your grave.

Behold, the one who brings our tidings of peace and proclaims good news is upon the mountains! O Judah, your adversary is utterly destroyed; from henceforth you shall not be passed over, and make your feasts, and celebrate your solemn assemblies.
The one who is relentless has come upon thee; guard thy heart, and prepare thy way, strengthen thy borders, and greatly increase thy power.
For the sorcerers have bewitched them, and they have cast away their wine; therefore, the Lord shall restore the glory of Jacob as the glory of Israel.

The mighty have clothed themselves in shame, and the strong have donned crimson garments. He also, on the day He prepares, shall cause the chariots to shake like the fire, and the soldiers shall be in disarray.
The chariots shall rattle upon the way, and the horsemen shall gallop; their appearance is as the flash of lightning, and they shall be as the burning flame.
They shall consider the mighty, and in their armor they shall be adorned; they shall swiftly emerge upon the wall, and the watchtower shall be prepared.
The gates of the maidens have been opened, and the house of the king has been uncovered.
The queen has been revealed, and she has been adorned; her maidservants are crying out like the pangs of childbirth, and they are smiting their breasts, saying, "Alas! Alas!"
Nineveh, however, was like a pool from her youth; now, however, they flee away, and they say, "Stand! Stand!" but there is none to return.
Her record has no end, and the number of her precious things cannot be counted; her silver is multiplied, and her gold is increased.
Desolate and waste is the land, and the heart is faint; the strong men have been weakened, and in every corner there is pain; the faces of all men are ashen.
The place where the lions roam, where the lion's roar is heard, and where the lion and lioness walk without fear, what is that place?
The lion has torn apart what is sufficient for its cubs, and for the beasts it has broken their bones, and its den is filled with prey.

Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; I will cut off thy chariots, and the sword of thy lions shall devour thee; I will destroy thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.
Woe to the city of blood! It is full of lies and robbery; it does not depart from its filth.
The voice of the slain, the voice of the oppressor, the neighing of horses, and the clamor of swift chariots have been heard.
The horseman is seen, the sword is drawn, the spear is brandished; the slain are many, and the wounded are in great pain; their bodies do not perish, for they are piled upon one another.
Concerning the slain, this is what has happened: she is greatly increased in her harlotry, and she has given her hand to the nations, and her children have been scattered.
Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; I will uncover thy skirts before thy face, and I will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
I will cast abominations upon thee, and I will make thee vile, and I will set thee as a spectacle.
All who see thee shall flee from thee, saying: "Nineveh is laid waste! Who will bemoan her? Where shall I seek comforters for thee?"
Thou art situated among the rivers, surrounded by waters; thy fortress is in the sea, and thy wall is in the sea. Yet dost thou not consider that thou art laid waste?
Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was without measure; they were thy helpers.
Yet she became a harlot, and her children were dashed to pieces at every corner; they were cast out like refuse in the streets, and her mighty ones were captured in the snare.
Thou also shalt be forsaken, and thou shalt be desolate; thou shalt seek a refuge from thine enemies.
All the trees of the field shall yield their first ripe fruit as the fig trees do; if they be shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the devourer.
Behold, the women of thy people that are in the midst of thee; the gates of thy land are opened wide unto thine enemies, and fire hath consumed thy fortresses.
For they shall trouble thee and bring forth water; they shall gather thy harvest, and into the dust shall they cast thee, and the instruments of thy trade shall they take away.
There shall the fire consume thee, the sword shall destroy thee; as the locust doth devour, so shall it consume thee, even as the caterpillar doth consume.
Thy merchants shall be more than the stars of heaven; the locust shall be scattered, and the grasshopper shall be abundant.

As for thee, thy lovers shall be as the flower; thy princes shall be as the grasshoppers, which in the cold day abide within the walls, but when the sun cometh forth, they shall flee away; their place shall not be known.
O king of Assyria, thy shepherds have slumbered; thy nobles are at rest; thy people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is none to gather them.
Thy destruction shall not be averted; thy wickedness is great; and all that hear thy tidings shall clap their hands over thee; for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
